To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the number of communication rounds required to find an $O(\epsilon)$-accurate solution is at least $\Omega(\frac{1}{\epsilon})$, and (ii) there exist algorithms that attain this lower bound.
we establish {\em optimal lower bounds} for smooth and strongly convex decentralized optimization over time-varying networks and design {\em optimal decentralized algorithms} that attain them.

(a) we establish the first lower bounds for the considered problem, (b) we show that the lower bound for the case when access is assumed to the dual gradients cannot be improved, (c) we show that a lower bound for the other case can be improved, and (d) we design an algorithm that achieves the lower bound.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of decentralized algorithms and lower bounds for the problem of minimizing a sum of smooth and strong convex functions, stored in a decentralized network whose links are changing over time.

two fundamental questions: (i) what is the minimum amount of communication and computation required to solve a given decentralized optimization problem, and (ii), given a solution, how can we find it in an optimal manner.

the following three contributions: (i) we provide the first lower bounds on the communication complexity of the decentralized optimization task; (ii) we design the first optimal algorithms that achieve these lower bounds; (iii) we show that our algorithms outperform state-of-the-art approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ADOM+ is the optimal algorithm in the sense that it achieves the best known performance for the considered problem.
the new ADOM+ algorithm is the first algorithm that is provably optimal for decentralized optimization with time-varying communication graphs.

ADOM+ and ADOM with the multi-consensus subroutine are the best algorithms for decentralized optimization in the smooth strongly convex case, and ADOM+ is the best algorithm for decentralized optimization in case the primal gradients are accessible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide {\em the first optimal algorithms} for decentralized optimization over time-varying networks.
we provide the first lower bounds and optimal algorithms for the problem of decentralized optimization of strongly convex functions.
we establish the first lower bounds for this fundamental problem, and we design two optimal algorithms, which outperform existing methods in terms of communication and computation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of time-varying networks, ADOM+ can be significantly more efficient than ADOM.
, in order to obtain optimal performance, the algorithms should be designed in a {\em multi-consensus} manner.
ADOM+ can be orders-of-magnitude faster than ADOM, and is competitive with the best existing algorithms for the problem at hand.
